claims.text: Tailoring the concentrations of lightweight elements such as Al and Ti in a multicomponent HEA can induce a uniformly distorted solid-solution matrix.
Processing the composition under suitable conditions can produce a uniform dispersion of nanoscale precipitates.
Lattice distortion increases the energetic driving force for coherent nanoscale precipitate formation.
Nanoscale precipitates strengthen the alloy by impeding dislocation motion.
Nanoscale precipitates strengthen the alloy through grain-boundary pinning.
The precipitates promote formation of a protective, self-passivating surface oxide.
The protective oxide improves both corrosion resistance and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Insufficient lattice distortion results in a lack of useful precipitate formation.
Excessive lattice distortion causes elemental segregation or precipitate coarsening.
Segregation associated with excessive distortion weakens the alloy.
Relative to the near-equimolar baseline, the optimized HEA will have higher yield strength.
Relative to the near-equimolar baseline, the optimized HEA will have higher tensile strength.
Relative to the baseline, the optimized HEA will exhibit lower corrosion current density.
Relative to the baseline, the optimized HEA will exhibit slower oxidation weight gain in TGA.
The optimized HEA will retain low density while realizing the mechanical and environmental improvements.
The strength-passivation synergy should operate at moderate to high service temperatures and regular strain rates.
Sufficiently high thermal exposure will coarsen or dissolve the nanoscale precipitates and eliminate the proposed synergy.
Severe strain rates can trigger detrimental phase transformations, including excessive FCC-to-BCC transformation.
A conventional near-equimolar control lacking targeted lightweight-element modulation will have inadequate distortion or inhomogeneous phases and inferior properties.
Al- or Ti-related compositional modification is known to induce stable nanoscale precipitates suitable for the proposed HEA design.
